lines.text: Why does that pair of sneakers you looked at once on Amazon follow you onto Instagram, YouTube, and news sites?
This marketing tactic is called retargeting, and it is powered by an invisible bidding auction.
When you browse a product, the website drops a tracking pixel or first-party cookie in your browser.
This pixel tags your browser with a unique anonymous user identifier.
Whenever you visit an entirely different website, ad exchange networks recognize your tracking ID.
In milliseconds, automated algorithms conduct a lightning auction, selling that ad banner to the sneaker brand for pennies.
Clear your browser cache and cookies regularly to shake off the ad trackers following you.
